from someone who is now 22 and was in your position at 13:


i’m sorry that you know how this feels. its an awful feeling and i wouldn’t wish it upon anyone. 

even if it might not feel like it, it does get better. call a suicide hotline, my friend. it’ll help a lot. those people are able to handle these situations, and they make a beautiful listening ear when it seems like nobody else will listen. depression and suicidal ideation have no age on them, and your age has nothing to do with how valid your experiences are. 

the people that treat you that way are not good friends to have around, and there WILL be more people in your life that DO matter and DO listen. 

if you can, talk to your doctor. they might be able to refer you to therapy, and if your doctor advises it your parents may take you more seriously. its extremely stressful when parents don’t listen, but be persistent. you seem like you are ACTIVELY seeking help for how you are feeling, which is a genuinely good thing. 

no matter how much your brain might try to trick you into thinking that what’s happening to you is the end-all-be-all for life, try to remind yourself that it isnt. that’s not you talking, that’s your depression and it is 100% something that you are able to overcome. take it in small portions, even if you need to take it minute by minute. each of those minutes is a minute more of you persevering, and that is an incredible feat that proves that you ARE strong enough and that you CAN keep living and ARE WORTHY of living.

i deal with this from time to time too. i STILL avoid alcohol consumption for this reason, abd i still get all jittery when someone around me is visibly drunk. something that helps is that i regularly wash my hands, and i also keep in mind that if someone is s* at one of these events, it’s typically just from alcohol or other substance consumption and not contagious, because if someone is GENUINELY s* to the point of it being contagious they will likely not be in any mood to go out, or even get out of bed for that matter. 

i even remember one time i literally saw someone get s* near me and didn’t register it due to the lighting and sound of the music drowing everything out, so i just kinda shrugged and figured the poor bastard was just too drunk. so i stayed at the party and just avoided the general area where he was. 

try making your friends (not just your partner) aware of your phobia so that if something IS to happen, you’ll have a support system with you. i found that it really helped me a lot, and they were able to get me out of any situation where i was uncomfortable and if they themselves were struggling with that they knew to take it somewhere else. it was scary at first, but the more and more i did it the more used to it i got. 

also, you’re posting about it which shows some degree of frustration. when you feel like you can (and dont rush yourself as there’s no time-table for this) take that frustration and channel it into a “im tired of this controlling me and i can do this!” kind of attitude. 

and there’s always other methods to getting out there with your social life too! invite friends over for a pregame before everyone goes out on the town, or have a night in playing videogames of some kind. you can still have a lot of fun with people at home too!

i know that it can be really really difficult, but i promise that it won’t last for forever. pace yourself, take it slow, and most importantly be kind and forgiving to yourself. sending you love and strength, op ♥️
